text: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
He grew up before him like a young shoot, like a root out of dry ground. He had no beauty, no majesty to draw our eyes, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.
He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom people hide their faces, he was despised, and we held him of no account.
Yet it was our griefs he bore, our sorrows he carried; but we considered him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us peace was laid upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.
All of us have strayed like sheep; each one has turned to his own way. And the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

versions.text: We all, like sheep, have gone astray; each of us has turned to his own way. And the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
versions.explanation: For oral reading, the double comma break in "We all, like sheep, have gone astray" interrupts the rhythm. Placing the simile after the verb gives a smoother spoken line while keeping the Hebrew sense exactly.

text: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb led to the slaughter, like a sheep silent before its shearers, he did not open his mouth.
By oppression and judgment he was taken away. And who of his generation gave it a thought? For he was cut off from the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people.
They assigned him a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was there any deceit in his mouth.

Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer. When he makes his life a guilt offering, he will see his offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
Out of the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.

versions.text: After the anguish of his soul he will see the light and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text supplied here reads simply "he will see, he will be satisfied" — the word "light" is not present in this text form (it appears in some ancient witnesses). Either drop "the light" as suggested, or retain it with a footnote such as: "Some ancient manuscripts and versions read 'he will see light'." As it stands, the added word is untagged content.

versions.text: After the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.
versions.explanation: The preposition on מֵעֲמַל is causal/source ("out of, as a result of") as much as temporal; "Out of" preserves the sense that the seeing and satisfaction arise from the suffering itself, rather than merely following it in time. It also reads slightly more smoothly aloud with the following clause. A footnote could helpfully note the textual variant: "Some ancient manuscripts and versions read 'he will see light'."

text: Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.
